## Pull request overview

Introduces a namespace-based system-object naming approach by adding an optional `namespace` to `ObjectSchema`, auto-deriving `tableName` from `{namespace}_{name}`, and adding/expanding canonical `sys_*` object definitions across auth/security/audit plugins.

**Changes:**
- Add `ObjectSchema.namespace` with `ObjectSchema.create()` auto-deriving `tableName` as `{namespace}_{name}`.
- Expand `SystemObjectName` constants and tests; update auth schema mappings to use the constants.
- Add new `sys` namespace object definitions for plugin-auth/plugin-security and introduce a new plugin-audit package exporting `SysAuditLog`.

The Unreleased section now contains two consecutive "### Changed" headings (one starting at line 26 and another at line 35). This breaks Keep-a-Changelog formatting and makes it unclear which bullets belong to which section. Please merge these into a single "### Changed" section (or otherwise restructure the headings) so there's only one "Changed" block per release section.

The new `namespace` docs say it must be a "single lowercase word" and the test descriptions below also imply alpha-only, but the regex `/^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$/` allows digits after the first character. Please either tighten the regex to match the stated constraint, or update the docs to explicitly allow lowercase alphanumerics.

Test description says namespace "must be lowercase alpha", but the actual schema regex allows digits (e.g. `sys2`). Please align the test wording with the implemented validation (or change the regex if alpha-only is intended).

In this section, the table column is labeled "Protocol Name" but the values shown (e.g. `sys_user`) are described elsewhere in the section as the *physical table name* auto-derived from `{namespace}_{name}`. Consider renaming the column to something like "Physical Table" / "Derived Table Name" to avoid confusing protocol identifiers with storage names. Also, since this section now describes a namespace-based convention, the section title still referencing a "sys_ Prefix" is misleading.
